smell: phase.WithRecorder and the install Phase's logutil.NopProgressReporter default exist as functional options on BasePhase, but okd.Provisioner sets them by writing the embedded BasePhase.Recorder field and install.Phase.Reporter field directly (okd.go:L138/L147-L148/L156). Net effect: the option exists, no caller uses it, and the struct fields are intentionally exported to enable post-construction mutation — a hand-written workaround for the option discoverability the constructor is supposed to provide.
evidence:
// okd.go:137
setupPhase := setup.New(p.executor, p.logger, p.version)
setupPhase.Recorder = p.recorder
setupPhase.BinDir = phase.ResolveBinDir(cfg)
...
// install:
installPhase.Recorder = p.recorder
installPhase.Reporter = p.reporter
fix_summary: Either thread Recorder/Reporter into each phase.New as functional options (matches the api:beabab0c fix) and drop the public Recorder/Reporter fields, or remove phase.WithRecorder since nothing calls it. Don't ship both. If WithRecorder stays for a future caller, document the future usage in MEMORY.md §scaffolding so the next audit recognises it.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Mutability (don't expose mutable fields when constructor options exist)

smell: executor.WithInheritedEnv has no callers in the production tree — every executor.New call goes through WithEnv, WithWorkDir, or WithLogger. The function exists as a documented escape hatch ('a tool that consumes a variable not on the allowlist') but no such tool currently exists.
fix_summary: Verify intent. WithInheritedEnv is shaped like a symmetric API to WithEnv — keep under MEMORY.md §scaffolding. If the doctor or debug-bundle tooling will eventually need to spawn a process with the full env (e.g. a wrapper that consumes NO_PROXY in a custom form), promote that intent in roadmap.md so the next audit recognises it.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (executor is the canonical subprocess runner)

smell: `IsRegistered(name)` has no callers in the tree. Symmetric with Get/Names/All so it qualifies as scaffolding under MEMORY.md §scaffolding — a future `okdctl addon validate` or wizard pre-check would naturally use it. Mark intent rather than delete.
fix_summary: Verify intent: grep roadmap for an addon-validate / wizard prerequisite item that needs IsRegistered. If none, leave as-is (scaffolding stays per MEMORY.md). Do not delete.
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API stays — symmetric with Get/Names/All)

smell: StepCleanupFirewall.SkipWhen calls `firewall.DetectBackend(context.Background(), p.Log)`. The justification comment claims the probe is bounded, but DetectBackend invokes `ufw status` and `system.IsServiceActive(ctx, "firewalld")`, both of which spawn systemctl/ufw subprocesses. systemctl is known to hang on a wedged systemd; with Background instead of the run ctx, a Ctrl-C during a stuck probe leaves SkipWhen blocked indefinitely and wedges the orchestrator's serial step loop.
severity_reason: the comment overstates the boundedness; in practice destroy SkipWhen runs in <1s on healthy hosts. Filed as minor because a stuck systemctl during destroy is a real (if rare) operator scenario and the fix is mechanical.
fix_summary: Capture the orchestrator's running ctx at the destroySteps call site by adding ctx as a parameter to (p *Phase).destroySteps and threading it into the SkipWhen closure: `SkipWhen: trackSkip("firewall", func() bool { return opts.SkipFirewall || firewall.DetectBackend(ctx, p.Log) == firewall.None })`. Phase.Execute already has ctx in hand at the BuildSteps boundary.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency: context.Background() in production code needs a justification comment
Go proverb: pass contexts; never store them
must_preserve: the SkipReason text; the trackSkip wrapping; opts.SkipFirewall short-circuit

smell: Phase.SetupClusterAccess accepts ctx but discards it via `_ context.Context`. The body chains AtomicWriteString on bashrc, CopyFileMode on kubeconfig, ChownToInvokingUser, Lstat checks, and a final addKubeconfigToBashrc — file IO that runs as the final install step, after a 60-minute install monitor. A Ctrl-C between MonitorInstallation returning and SetupClusterAccess completing will not interrupt the bashrc write because no inner call honours ctx.
severity_reason: file IO in this body is bounded in practice; the install path's other steps (SetupKubeconfig at install/phase.go:166) thread ctx so the asymmetry is the smell, not a hang risk.
fix_summary: Rename the parameter to `ctx context.Context` and add `if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil { return err }` between the four logical sub-steps (kubeconfig copy, chown, bashrc), matching the pattern in install.SetupKubeconfig at flux.go:166-169 and ignition.ValidateIgnitionFiles. Alternative: document the ctx-ignored choice with a symmetric-API comment matching the proxmox.Connect/Disconnect doc at proxmox.go:88-89.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency: every goroutine needs a stop signal or documented leak bound (extends to ctx-accepting funcs)
must_preserve: the symlink-refusal lstat in addKubeconfigToBashrc; the CopyFileMode 0o600 invariant on kubeconfig

smell: startMetricsServer formats the SplitHostPort error into Msg with %s instead of carrying it via Err: errors.Is/As against the underlying net.AddrError is impossible downstream because the chain is broken. The error reaches root.go's exitCodeFor where the AddrError can never be inspected.
fix_summary: Move err into the Err field: &errtypes.ConfigError{Msg: fmt.Sprintf("invalid --metrics-addr %q", addr), Err: err}. Drops the duplicated message tail, preserves the chain.
rule_source: Go stdlib §errors: wrap with %w (or carry via field) to preserve identity
must_preserve: errtypes.ConfigError type so exit 2 still applies

smell: install.sh declares and expands a bash array (`_gh_auth_header=()` / `${_gh_auth_header[@]}`) but the README and install.sh's own usage docstring direct users to pipe the script into `sh`. On Debian/Ubuntu where `/bin/sh` is `dash`, the script syntax-errors at the array declaration before any download starts, leaving the user with a cryptic `Syntax error: "(" unexpected` instead of an installed binary. The shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash` is ignored when the script is read via stdin by `sh`.
evidence:
# README / docstring: curl -sSfL .../install.sh | sh
_gh_auth_header=()
if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    _gh_auth_header=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN")
fi
VERSION=$(curl ... "${_gh_auth_header[@]}" ...)
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path-equivalent — install.sh is the documented entry point and silently fails on the dominant Linux distros (Debian/Ubuntu/derivatives) where /bin/sh is dash; users hit a cryptic syntax error during the published one-liner install and may retry blind or fall back to unverified manual binary fetches.
fix_summary: Either (a) replace the README invocation with `| bash` (and update the install.sh docstring on line 10), matching helm.sh and k3s.io patterns; or (b) make the auth header POSIX-compatible by inlining the conditional: `if [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then VERSION=$(curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" ...); else VERSION=$(curl ...); fi`. Option (a) is one character per doc site and matches the shebang's intent.
rule_source: ShellCheck SC3030 (in POSIX sh, arrays are undefined)
repo-counter-example: scripts/install.sh:1 (#!/usr/bin/env bash declares bash, README pipes to sh)
must_preserve: the GITHUB_TOKEN rate-limit-lift behavior; cosign + sha256 verification chain

smell: The `curl_safe` wrapper centralizes hardened curl flags (HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 floor, connect/transfer timeouts, retry policy), but the latest-release resolution call does not use it — it inlines a partial subset of those flags. The retry-on-connrefused behavior the wrapper provides is silently absent at exactly the call site most likely to fail (GitHub API rate-limit / transient 5xx).
evidence:
curl_safe() { curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 --retry 2 --retry-connrefused "$@"; }
...
VERSION=$(curl -sSfL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 \
    "${_gh_auth_header[@]}" \
    "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" | ...)
fix_summary: Replace the inline curl with `curl_safe -sSfL --max-time 30 "${_gh_auth_header[@]}" "..."`. The wrapper's `--max-time 120` is overridden by the second `--max-time 30` (curl uses last value). Net change: ~3 lines.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: scripts/install.sh:38 (curl_safe defined for exactly this purpose)
Go proverb: a little copying is better than a little dependency — but only when copies stay in sync

smell: The lint-shell job restricts shellcheck's `scandir` to `./scripts` only, so `.github/scripts/coverage-check.sh` (an 82-line bash script with associative arrays, process substitution, and bc-based arithmetic running in CI) is never linted. Any shellcheck-class regression in coverage-check.sh — quoting bug, unguarded var expansion, broken associative-array key — slips past CI and only manifests as a confusing CI failure when the floor logic mis-triggers.
evidence:
lint-shell:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@...
      - uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@... # 2.0.0
        with:
          severity: warning
          scandir: "./scripts"
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — coverage-check.sh gates the test-go job, so a silent break here either fails CI cryptically or, worse, lets a coverage regression slip if a quoting bug zeroes a parsed value.
fix_summary: Drop the `scandir: "./scripts"` line so action-shellcheck scans the whole tree (its default), or set `scandir: "."` explicitly. Optionally add `additional_files: ".github/scripts"` if you want to keep `./scripts` as the primary path. Net effect: one less line of config; coverage-check.sh becomes lint-protected.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §tooling — `lint-yaml`, `validate-terraform` etc. all in CI; lint-shell should match scope
ShellCheck wiki — recommended for any non-trivial shell script
must_preserve: the action-shellcheck SHA pin and version trailer

smell: `environments/production/variables.tf` ships hardcoded defaults that look operator-specific: `target_node = "pve01"`, `cluster_name = "grappleberry"`, `vmid_base = 7000`. terraform.tfvars is gitignored, but anyone running `terraform apply` without overrides would deploy with these defaults silently. The `production` directory name implies this is the canonical example for prod deploys; defaults should be intentionally absent for variables with no sensible cross-environment value, so terraform errors with `target_node is required`.
fix_summary: For variables with no sensible cross-environment default (target_node, cluster_name, vmid_base), drop the `default` attribute so terraform fails fast with a missing-required error. Keep defaults on infrastructure shape vars (cpu_cores, memory_mb). Net change: ~5 deletions in variables.tf.
rule_source: HashiCorp Terraform docs — Input Variables: "If no default is set, the variable is required"
tflint terraform_required_version + terraform_required_providers preset (already enabled at .tflint.hcl:9)
must_preserve: the variable types and validation behavior in the module

smell: The production environment's variables redeclare every module variable but drop the `validation` blocks present on the module (cpu_cores 2-32, memory_mb >= 8192, master_count odd 1-5, vmid_base 100-9000, etc.). The module's validation will fire eventually but only AFTER terraform plan resolves the module reference, producing later/less-pinpointed errors. The duplicated-but-loosened variables here are a missed early-validation opportunity and create two specs that can drift.
fix_summary: Either (a) delete the duplicated env-level vars and let the module own validation (the env's main.tf passes them straight through anyway); or (b) mirror the module's validation blocks here for fail-fast errors. Option (a) is the smaller diff and aligns with module-as-source-of-truth.
rule_source: HashiCorp Terraform docs — Input Variables (validation precondition vs module precondition)
must_preserve: the env's variable surface that callers (operators / CI) depend on by name

smell: ssh-keyscan is invoked with the host extracted from the user-supplied flux.repository URL. The scp-style fallback `gitHost("git@-arg:path")` returns `-arg`, which ssh-keyscan parses as a flag, enabling argument injection (CWE-88). ValidateSettings only checks scheme prefix, not the host shape.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path: argv-injection of an unauthenticated network probe via a config-controlled value; scp-style URL handling allows a leading dash to bypass URL parser conventions.
fix_summary: Reject host strings beginning with `-` in gitHost (or pass `--` separator before the host: `RunChecked(ctx, "ssh-keyscan", "--", host)` if ssh-keyscan supports it; otherwise validate against an idn-like character set first). Add the same guard in ValidateSettings so wizard input is rejected up front.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §security-invariants — allowlist > denylist on critical paths

smell: Temp file path is built from os.TempDir() and os.Getpid() — a predictable name (`/tmp/haproxy-<pid>.cfg`). Although /tmp's sticky bit and the root re-exec model block non-root takeover today, the canonical helper system.WriteTempFile (per CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes) avoids the predictable-name footgun and centralises the secure-temp pattern.
fix_summary: Replace the predictable name + AtomicWriteString with system.WriteTempFile("haproxy-*.cfg", 0o644, writer) to use the canonical mode-at-open temp helper.

smell: installBinary uses os.CreateTemp + immediate Close + later download.Download writing to that path. Bypasses the canonical system.WriteTempFile per CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes. Combined with sec:21dc1103 (download.Download lacks O_NOFOLLOW), the create-then-rewrite path runs as root with a temp file mode established by os.CreateTemp's default — fine today but fragile against future caller errors.
fix_summary: Refactor to system.WriteTempFile so all binary downloads thread through the canonical helper. Pair with sec:21dc1103 (add O_NOFOLLOW in download.fetchToFile).

smell: verifyKubeVIPAPIHealthBootstrap falls back to InsecureSkipVerify when the kubeconfig CA is unavailable, even outside the documented x509.HostnameError window. The CA-unavailable branch (line 234) silently disables TLS verification end-to-end for kube-vip api health probes — a probe that decides whether to advance state. An attacker with bastion-network access could spoof :6443 healthz responses to advance the kube-vip handoff path during postinstall.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path: TLS-skip on the kube-vip health probe gates handoff and (via update-ingress) HAProxy teardown; a forged 'ok' response advances destructive state machine. CWE-295.
fix_summary: Make CA-pool retrieval failure a hard error in postinstall (the kubeconfig MUST exist by then) or, at minimum, disable the HAProxy-removal advancement when CA is unavailable. Keep the x509.HostnameError-only fallback (the documented kube-vip cert re-issue window) but remove the unconditional CA-missing fallback.

smell: RemoveHAProxy probes /healthz on the kube-vip with InsecureSkipVerify when KubeconfigCAPool fails. Same pattern as sec:1e8ffb91 — the probe outcome is load-bearing because it gates the HAProxy teardown. CA unavailable post-install should be a hard error, not a TLS-skip.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path: same TLS-skip-on-CA-miss pattern as sec:1e8ffb91, on a code path that decides whether to remove the bastion-side HAProxy load balancer.
fix_summary: Return a typed error when the CA pool is unavailable; do not fall back to NewInsecure for credential-bearing probes that gate destructive state changes. Cross-link with sec:1e8ffb91 — both sites should be fixed together.

smell: AtomicWrite calls os.CreateTemp(dir, ".tmp-*") which opens the temp file with mode 0o600 (Go default), then later calls os.Chmod(tmpPath, perm). For perm tighter than 0o600 (rare in this repo), the create-then-chmod window is benign because the file starts tighter. For perm wider (0o644 for haproxy.cfg, dnsmasq.conf), the temp file is briefly readable only to owner (root under sudo). The pattern only becomes a problem if a future caller passes 0o600 expecting the helper guarantees it; today the helper happens to satisfy that.
fix_summary: Switch to OpenFile(tmpPath, O_RDWR|O_CREATE|O_EXCL, perm) to apply mode at open time (mirroring system.openTempFile in the same file at line 77). Eliminates the Chmod-window concern and aligns with the canonical CopyFileMode pattern.

smell: NewInsecure exists as a public constructor on the httputil surface. Three sites call it (postinstall/verify.go x2, postinstall/haproxy.go x1) — sec:1e8ffb91 and sec:761e5126 are per-site; this is the policy umbrella. Making the insecure-client constructor part of the public API normalises its use; a future wizard or addon could reach for it without owning the security review.
fix_summary: Either move NewInsecure to an internal-only file (lowercase newInsecure) and surface the bootstrap-window probe via a higher-level helper that explicitly takes the kubeconfig path for CA fallback, OR add a build-tag-gated test that asserts no caller outside postinstall/ imports it. Forces future callers to add the TLS-skip rationale to the policy review.

smell: processTarEntry calls os.MkdirAll with the archive-supplied mode (header.Mode & 0o777). If the archive declares 0o777 on a directory containing sensitive files, the directory is created world-writable. Subsequent file writes use O_NOFOLLOW (good), but a parallel attacker who can write into the world-writable extracted dir between MkdirAll and the subsequent file extraction could plant files that survive the extraction.
fix_summary: Mask the archive-supplied directory mode against 0o755 (clear group/world write bits) before passing to MkdirAll. Aligns with tar(1) --no-same-permissions and matches the install.sh extraction flag.

smell: Master resource has no `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. The block comment at line 244-246 acknowledges Terraform requires a literal boolean for prevent_destroy and recommends an override.tf as workaround — but the default ships unprotected. A rogue --target=module.okd_cluster.proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.master[N] passes the destroyTargetRE allowlist and destroys an etcd-quorum member with zero terraform-side guard. Roadmap iac:18a795d5 (deferred) covers this exactly.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss-risk: etcd quorum loss requires offline rebuild from cluster-backup; a typo'd --target on master[N] is single-keystroke catastrophic. Defense-in-depth at the HCL layer is the single highest-value guard.
fix_summary: Add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to the master resource literal-mode (drop the var dependency). For the legitimate okdctl destroy path, gate behind a separate module flavour or document the override.tf escape hatch in the destroy CLI's --help. Cross-reference roadmap iac:18a795d5:hcl-no-prevent-destroy-masters.
rule_source: Terraform best-practices: prevent_destroy on stateful resources

smell: remoteISO256 builds the remote ssh command via raw string concat ("sha256sum "+target where target = remotePath+"/"+filename), then calls phase.SSHRun which feeds the whole string to ssh's trailing arg — the remote login shell evaluates it. Sibling phase/iso_cleanup.go shellSingleQuote-wraps every atom; this site bypasses that template and accepts whatever metacharacters land in filename (filepath.Base of an ISO path derived from cluster machine names that flow from config).
evidence:
target := remotePath + "/" + filename
result, err := phase.SSHRun(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum "+target)
severity_reason: Config-controlled value (machine name → ISO filename) flows unescaped into a remote shell evaluation; the canonical sibling pattern (iso_cleanup.go shellSingleQuote) exists to prevent exactly this — rubric §4/known-exploit-path adjacent.
fix_summary: Switch to phase.SSHRunArgv(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum", "--", target) — argv mode still hands ssh a joined command but each atom is preserved verbatim, and a leading -- guards filenames starting with -. Or, mirror iso_cleanup.go: phase.SSHRun(ctx, exec, host, "sha256sum -- "+shellSingleQuote(target)).
rule_source: internal/distribution/okd/phase/ssh.go:L43-L48 doc: argv mode does NOT bypass the shell
must_preserve: phase.SSHRun and phase.SSHRunArgv are canonical wrappers — don't introduce a third ssh helper; use the existing argv-mode helper.
